page: Amazon Web Services r8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance configured with 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs via Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running up to 3.9 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this bare-metal platform provides direct hardware execution without virtualization hypervisor overhead. The compute architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 1,536 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, providing 8.0 GB per physical core to support extreme in-memory footprints.

Storage and network provisions are sized to match the compute and memory density. The instance includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, enabling high-throughput and low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 75 Gbps, ensuring fast inter-node communication and data ingestion across distributed environments without public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional multi-core performance, achieving top-tier status in stress-ng multi-threaded tests at 209,065.42 and Geekbench multi-core runs at 22,433.0. Memory throughput is characterized by a top-tier read bandwidth of 15,491.12 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 585.22 GB/sec across larger 256 MB blocks. Database transaction capacity is notable, evidenced by top-tier results in PassMark database benchmarks and 240.29 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Additionally, the instance delivers solid performance across CPU-based LLM inference tasks utilizing its integrated AMX instructions.

From a resource and qualitative cost perspective, r8id.metal-48xl presents a high-density, bare-metal consolidation target. The dedicated allocation eliminates multi-tenant noisy neighbor contention and virtualization latency. However, utilizing non-persistent local NVMe instance store requires external replication mechanisms to guarantee data persistence across hardware stops. This server is best suited for memory-bound relational databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, big data ETL processing, and low-latency static web serving pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor reaching clock speeds of 3.9 GHz. The server provides 1,536 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, delivering an 8.0 GB per physical core density, alongside 11,400 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and 75 Gbps baseline network throughput. Hardware-level acceleration includes AVX-512 and Intel AMX, allowing for strong multi-threaded execution and CPU-based inference workloads. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core computational throughput, robust memory bandwidth exceeding 585 GB/sec on uncached reads, and outstanding database transactional capabilities, including 240.29 million Redis operations per second. Lacking hypervisor overhead, it offers dedicated performance for memory-intensive enterprise databases, large-scale caching layers, real-time analytics, and data-intensive pipelines requiring direct hardware access.
